Supreme Council · Beginner guide

Ask one question, read separately generated AI answers and decide which claims deserve a closer look.

Who can use it

People weighing a decision who are comfortable with a command line and provider accounts.

How to get it

The public v0.1 guide covers Windows and Python 3.10 or newer. Follow its isolated environment setup and configure an eligible provider account. Newer development builds have no verified public download here.

Your first session

Keep credentials in the local .env file. Confirm that the provider account and exact models qualify for its free tier. Review the selected models and submit a short, non-sensitive prompt when ready.

What you can do

  • The public CLI documentation describes OpenRouter and optional Groq and Gemini setup. Free-tier eligibility, quotas and costs depend on provider terms and the account. Local limits cannot verify billing.
  • Compare the individual answers and optionally request a synthesis. Agreement can still contain errors. Check important claims yourself.

Data and backups

Prompts go to selected providers, which may retain them. Reports are saved locally as readable files. Copy reports you want to keep to a private backup and keep API keys separate.
